behavioral_effects: EMAIL_PROVIDER=resend with RESEND_API_KEY selects ResendProvider; EMAIL_PROVIDER=smtp with SMTP_HOST selects SMTPProvider with host, port, credentials, and TLS from settings
Missing credentials or unknown provider values fall back to the log provider with a logged warning instead of silently
LOG_PROVIDER_WRITE_TO_DISK, previously read but never passed, now reaches LogProvider - same config-read-but-not-honored defect in the same function
compatibility_impact: Behavioral: environments that already set EMAIL_PROVIDER=resend or smtp were silently getting the log provider and will start actually sending mail on deploy of this change. Unknown provider values now log a warning instead of silently degrading. New deps resend and aiosmtplib added to backend
follow_up: Curate the secret classification for RESEND_API_KEY and SMTP_PASSWORD when the phase-3 secret-classification-is-curated rule is enforced
limitations: No live send was tested against Resend or an SMTP server; selection and construction are unit-tested, delivery is not
reason: get_email_provider matches 'case log | _' so EMAIL_PROVIDER=resend or smtp silently receives the log provider and no mail is ever sent despite the resend and smtp provider modules existing; the config is read but never honored
risks: Environments with EMAIL_PROVIDER set will begin real mail delivery; operators must verify the value before deploying
rollback: Revert the commit and run uv sync in backend to drop the two new packages; provider selection returns to always-log
security_impact: Two new secret-bearing settings (RESEND_API_KEY, SMTP_PASSWORD) join the backend config; they default to unset, are never logged, and .env.example carries placeholders only. The generated configuration manifest classifies them runtime pending the phase-3 curated secret classification
summary: Honor EMAIL_PROVIDER: select the resend and smtp providers instead of silently falling back to log
